new_statements.rule_in_words: Survey-wide convention covering all of Laycock's 1967 Lumi-area wordlists, including 'Aiku (.. Umbrak-Aiku)' = the Aiku cluster to which Ambrak then belonged: stress is non-phonemic and falls by default on the first syllable whose vowel is not schwa; it is written only when it falls elsewhere. In the published Aiku list (46 items on TransNewGuinea.org) one form is marked, yimán 'breast', the rest unmarked. Not an Ambrak-specific statement and not a phonological analysis.
new_statements.exceptions: Stress on other than the first non-schwa syllable is marked with an acute (Aiku list: yimán 'breast'); schwa-initial words (mərəŋkil 'moon', təkŋan 'sun', təŋkarwak 'white') are implicitly stressed on the first full-vowel syllable. Laycock says no consistency should be expected in the transcription.
new_statements.domain_note: Isolated citation forms from ~220-item survey wordlists elicited at Nuku in July 1967 (Aiku informant 'NR' = not recorded); a blanket statement over c. 60 languages of the Lumi Subdistrict, not a description of Ambrak.
new_statements.identity_note: Ambrak [aag] (Glottolog ambr1239) was part of ISO 'Aiku' [mzf] (Glottolog bookkeeping aiku1240) until CR 2006-057 split it from Yangum Mon [ymo, yang1296], Yangum Dey [yde, yang1297] and Yangum Gel [ygl, yang1295] in 2007. Laycock 1968/1973 treat the whole cluster as one language 'Aiku' with the alternate name 'Umbrak-Aiku' (= Ambrak) and villages Monandin, Sengi, Suau (= Ambrak's Suwau), Womerau, Yirkin; his published Aiku wordlist (informant 'NR') is filed by Glottolog and TransNewGuinea under Yangum Mon, while PARADISEC indexes his Notebook C3 'Umbrak-Aiku' under both aag and ymo. The stress statement quoted is therefore a survey-wide transcription convention covering the pre-split Aiku cluster, not a statement about Ambrak (Suwau) specifically; whether the underlying data are Ambrak or Yangum Mon cannot be decided from what was accessible.
